title: [Forecast quý 2/2025] Percentage of households with items
prompt: The graph shows the percentage of households in one country that had various goods between 2001 and 2008. Summarize the informtaion by describing the main features of the charts and making comparisons where appropriate.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the proportion of households that owned various household items in 2001 and 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the ownership of nearly all household goods increased over the given period, with only telephone ownership showing a decline. Additionally, items with initially low ownership rates demonstrated the most substantial growth, particularly internet access and mobile phones.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with items that had relatively high ownership rates, in 2001, telephones were present in 95% of households, significantly higher than microwaves at 80%, CD players at 70%, and clothes dryers at 60%. Microwaves demonstrated the clearest upward trend among this group, reaching 90% by 2008, a figure matched by CD players after a 20-point rise, while clothes dryers saw a more modest 10-point increase to 70%. Conversely, telephones were the only item in this group to decline, falling 5 points to 90%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding items with lower initial penetration, in 2001, home computers accounted for 40% of households, significantly higher than mobile phones at 20%, while internet access and dishwashers were each present in only 10% of homes. Home computers doubled to 80% by 2008, while mobile phones showed even more dramatic expansion, quadrupling from 20% to 80%. Internet access demonstrated the most significant relative increase, rising six-fold to 60%, alongside a substantial expansion in dishwasher ownership, which increased four-fold to 40% in the final year.
